freedoom1.wad.role: primary IWAD target (Doom-1-style content, matches the mission's preference)

freedoom.vendor_note: The .wad files themselves are NOT committed to this git repository (28MB each, large binary game-data assets) -- only this manifest, the SHA-256 hashes above, and the license/credits text (software/assets_manifest/freedoom_license/) are tracked. The actual freedoom1.wad used for any build/test must be re-fetched from the release_url above and its hash checked against the value recorded here before use; scripts/prepare_sd_image.py's --wad argument expects this file as a local path, not something it fetches itself.

pixel_format_finding.summary: DoomGeneric's TRUE native render resolution is 320x200 8-bit palette-indexed (I_VideoBuffer in doomgeneric/i_video.c), NOT the 640x400 32-bit DG_ScreenBuffer default. Setting #define CMAP256 and DOOMGENERIC_RESX=320/DOOMGENERIC_RESY=200 (matching SCREENWIDTH/SCREENHEIGHT exactly, giving fb_scaling=1) makes I_FinishUpdate's output path a direct memcpy of the indexed buffer into DG_ScreenBuffer -- i.e. DG_ScreenBuffer becomes exactly an 8-bit-indexed 320x200 (64,000-byte) frame, matching the mission's preferred framebuffer format exactly, once this specific combination of defines is used.
pixel_format_finding.verified_by: direct source inspection of software/upstream/doomgeneric/{doomgeneric.h,i_video.c} at the pinned commit, not assumed
source_citations: software/upstream/doomgeneric/doomgeneric.h: pixel_t is uint8_t under CMAP256, uint32_t otherwise
software/upstream/doomgeneric/i_video.c:290: I_VideoBuffer = Z_Malloc(SCREENWIDTH*SCREENHEIGHT,...) -- the real 8-bit indexed draw target
software/upstream/doomgeneric/i_video.c:282-284: fb_scaling = s_Fb.xres/SCREENWIDTH (and yres/SCREENHEIGHT, whichever is smaller)
software/upstream/doomgeneric/i_video.c:339-358: the I_FinishUpdate loop -- CMAP256 + fb_scaling==1 takes the plain memcpy branch, skipping cmap_to_fb's RGB conversion entirely
pixel_format_finding.remaining_open_item: I_SetPalette (i_video.c:388) updates a LOCAL colors[] table used only by cmap_to_fb's RGB-conversion path, which CMAP256 mode bypasses entirely -- meaning the game's dynamic palette changes (damage flash, berserk tint, etc.) need a separate path to reach the hardware's own palette RAM. Needs a small, documented patch to i_video.c's I_SetPalette (forwarding the palette bytes to a new platform hook) -- tracked in software/patches/, not yet written as of this manifest's creation.
